title: Grocery service details
description: One service in depth: health, HTTP endpoints, calls to other services, database pool, JVM, Kafka, logs.

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Prometheus can read the service's metrics.

panels.title: Health check
panels.description: /actuator/health answers UP (its database, Redis ... are reachable).

panels.title: Running for
panels.description: Time since the service started.

panels.title: Requests / s
panels.description: User requests per second (last 5 minutes).

panels.title: Server errors
panels.description: Share of the requests answered with 5xx (last 5 minutes).

panels.title: Response time p95
panels.description: 95 % of the requests were faster (last 5 minutes).

panels.title: Heap used
panels.description: Share of the maximum heap in use.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Share of the machine's CPU the service uses.

panels.title: Requests per second by endpoint
panels.description: The endpoint is the path pattern (ids are {placeholders}).

panels.title: Answers by status code
panels.description: 2xx = OK, 4xx = the client's mistake (validation, not found ...), 5xx = server error.

panels.title: Response time (all endpoints)
panels.description: 50 / 95 / 99 % of the requests were faster than this. The dots are sample requests: click one to open its trace in Jaeger.

panels.title: Response time p95 by endpoint
panels.description: Which endpoint is slow.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (method, uri, le) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{service="$service", uri!~"/actuator.*", uri!~"/api/v1/chat/messages|.*/stream"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Endpoints in the selected time range
panels.description: Sorted by the 95th percentile response time: the slowest endpoints first.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (method, uri, le) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{service="$service", uri!~"/actuator.*"}[$__range]))) >= 0

panels.title: Server errors by endpoint and exception
panels.description: Which endpoint fails and with which exception. The stack trace is in the service's ERROR log line (dashboard Grocery logs).

targets.expr: sum by (method, uri, exception) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service="$service", uri!~"/actuator.*", status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Calls to other services (per second)
panels.description: Outgoing HTTP calls (RestClient; for the gateway: the routes it forwards to). Failed connections show an exception other than none.

panels.title: Time of the calls to other services (average)
panels.description: How long the services this one depends on take to answer.

targets.expr: sum by (method, uri) (rate(http_client_requests_seconds_sum{service="$service", uri!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (method, uri) (rate(http_client_requests_seconds_count{service="$service", uri!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: active = running a query or transaction, idle = ready, pending = requests WAITING for a connection (should be 0), max = pool size.

panels.title: Waiting for a connection
panels.description: Average and longest time a request waited for a free connection, and timeouts (gave up after 30 s: the request failed). Alerts: DatabasePoolExhausted, DatabaseConnectionTimeouts.

panels.title: Repository calls: average time
panels.description: Time of each Spring Data repository method (one or more SQL queries; Elasticsearch in product-read-service). Slow ones are the first place to look for slow endpoints.

targets.expr: sum by (repository, method) (rate(spring_data_repository_invocations_seconds_sum{service="$service"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (repository, method) (rate(spring_data_repository_invocations_seconds_count{service="$service"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Heap memory
panels.description: used = objects in memory now; max = -Xmx. It drops at every garbage collection.

panels.title: Non-heap memory
panels.description: Memory outside the heap: loaded classes (Metaspace), compiled code, buffers.

panels.title: Garbage collection
panels.description: Share of time the JVM was paused for garbage collection, and pauses per minute. Alert: HighGcTime (> 10 %).

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: process = this service, system = the whole machine (both as a share of all CPUs).

panels.title: Threads
panels.description: live and daemon threads, and how many are blocked or waiting.

panels.title: Web threads (Tomcat)
panels.description: Threads handling requests: busy, existing, maximum, and the requests in progress. Busy near max = requests queue up. Alert: WebThreadsBusy. With virtual threads (spring.threads.virtual.enabled) Tomcat has no thread pool and reports -1: the thread lines are left out, 'in progress' still works (docs/performance.md). (Not for the gateway: it runs on Netty.)

panels.title: Events handled per second
panels.description: By listener and result. A failure is retried; after the last retry the event goes to <topic>.DLT.

panels.title: Time to handle one event (average)
panels.description: Includes the database work of the listener.

panels.title: Consumer lag (events behind)
panels.description: Events waiting in each topic for this service. 0 = up to date. Alert: KafkaConsumerLag (> 1000 for 10 minutes).

panels.title: Log lines per minute by level
panels.description: Counted by Logback. The lines themselves: Logs link at the top.

panels.title: Log lines not delivered to Loki
panels.description: dropped should stay 0 (a full 10 MB send queue: Loki was down too long). waiting = lines of the next batch (sent every 2 s); right after a start it briefly holds the start-up lines, which is normal.
